summary: The bill lets female college athletes sue their school or athletic association for damages if it negligently or recklessly allows a biological male to compete in a women's event and the female athlete is physically injured as a result.

scores.thoughts: The bill creates a private civil right of action but contains no provisions authorizing, expanding, or reducing any federal spending, appropriations, or budgetary outlays.
No tax provisions, rate changes, credits, or revenue measures appear in the bill.
The legislation addresses athletic competition rules and tort liability; it does not alter healthcare delivery, insurance, coverage mandates, or public/private healthcare structures.
The bill is silent on firearms, background checks, or gun regulations.
No immigration, visa, border, or citizenship provisions are present.
The text contains no references to reproductive rights, abortion access, or related medical procedures.
No defense, military, or national-security spending or policy changes are included.
The bill does not address environmental regulations, emissions, land use, or climate policy.
No welfare, entitlement, or social-services programs are modified or created.

While the bill imposes potential liability on institutions of higher education regarding athletic eligibility, it does not alter federal education funding, curriculum standards, school choice mechanisms, or public-school investment levels.
No drug enforcement, decriminalization, or controlled-substance provisions exist.
The bill establishes a civil cause of action rather than any criminal penalties, sentencing reforms, or policing measures.
No trade agreements, tariffs, or import/export rules are addressed.
The legislation has no fiscal impact on deficits or debt reduction.

The bill authorizes lawsuits against colleges and athletic associations that allow biological males to compete in female-only sports, thereby enforcing biological-sex categories and limiting the ability of transgender women to participate under gender-identity rules. This directly constrains legal protections and inclusion policies tied to gender identity.
No foreign-assistance or international-aid provisions are present.
The bill does not touch voting rights, election administration, or voter-ID requirements.
No technology regulation, data privacy, or platform-liability measures are included.
The legislation does not address collective bargaining, union rights, or workplace labor standards.
No religious exemptions, conscience clauses, or conflicts between civil-rights protections and religious liberty are addressed.
